activityGoals.name: Celsius To Fahrenheit Conversion
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that computes the Fahrenheit equivalent of an input Celsius value using the formula F = (9/5)C + 32. The input Celsius value is an integer.
activityGoals.correctOutput:
Enter the Celsius value: 
Celsius Temperature: 34
Fahrenheit Equivalent: 93.2

lineList.content: //Step 1: Define the data that we need for this program

commentList: The constant BASE in the conversion formula, we set it to 32. We define BASE as constant because 32 is a constant in the conversion formula.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.

The constant CONVERSION_FACTOR, we set it to 9.0/5. We define it as constant because this factor is a constant in the conversion formula. Note that at least one operand of the division operator must be a floating-point number to ensure that the fractional part of the number is kept.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.
We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the Celsius value.
We need to read the Celsius value that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the Celsius value by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.
